drawings.description: le même système de catégories redessiné en perspective : PB au sommet, PBCR, EPCR, PBC, EPC, et en bas PB $\to$ EP ; flèches « recoller collier », « recoller cône », « identité », « contraction $B$ » ; un mot biffé \ill{} à gauche.
drawings.kind: system of categories in perspective (arrow diagram)
drawings.notes: Nodes placed once as on the page: PB at the top, PBCR, EPCR, PBC, the EPC vertex, PB at the bottom, EP. The four arrows from the top PB leave from one point under the label: to PBCR (recoller collier, a double stroke), to EPCR (recoller cône), straight down to the bottom PB (identité), and to EP (contraction B). The straight line PB -> PB passes through the point where the arrows EPCR -> EPC and PBC -> EPC end (computed on it), and carries an arrowhead there and one at the bottom PB; the label EPC stands to the right of that point. Further arrows: PBCR -> EPCR, PBCR -> PBC, EPC -> EP (heavy), PBC -> bottom PB (heavy), bottom PB -> EP. The bottom node reads like "PD" on the facsimile; it is labelled PB after the transcription. Left out: the struck word at the left; a struck "ident" on the vertical line above EPCR; an inked blot between PBC and the bottom PB (a struck stroke); two small strokes like a V under "recoller collier"; a small double-headed stroke with letters (beta? d?) between EPC and EP, not readable. Still differs: those last two small marks. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the arrow labelled « identité » starts at the top PB and ends at the bottom node, so the bottom node is PB (its B is written like the B of the top label), and the vertical line is the one arrow PB -> PB, passing behind the point EPC where the arrows from EPCR and PBC end. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: un carré raturé, puis un carré à deux diagonales
drawings.kind: struck square, then a square with two diagonals
drawings.notes: A square with both diagonals heavy (the right one). Omitted as struck: the first square on the left, covered with crossing-out strokes (« un carré raturé »), its outline and the strokes alike. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): row (2'') reads 1 | 1 | square, the partition 1 + 1 + 4 of the six points, so one square stands for the four points: the first square, scrawled over by a stroke that runs out of its outline, is the false start redone at once on its right, and stays left out. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: petit carré à diagonale, en partie raturé
drawings.kind: small square with a diagonal, partly struck
drawings.notes: A small square with a heavy diagonal ending in two points and a small x inside, and a heavy vertical bar to its right. Omitted as struck: the scribble to the left of the square. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

Two ovals, the first with points (one heavy) marked 2 below, the second with three points marked 3. The first oval seems to hold three marks (one large, two small) where the transcription counts 2; the label 2 is his.

Two hatched triangles side by side: a long one with its apex at the left (vertices A, B at the top, C at the bottom right, each edge drawn between the same vertices) and a smaller one to its right (D, E, F), the dotted vertices thickened as on the page; a thin line runs from the apex A to the left vertex D of the second triangle. His hatching is a zigzag; it is drawn as a regular hatch. Still differs: a stroke from the top vertex B to a dot at the upper right (before the words "ce"), and a faint stroke from there towards E, which may close a third triangle B-dot-E, are left out as uncertain; the struck/overwritten letters on the left half of the first triangle are left out. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 700 dpi a solid stroke runs from the top vertex B to a full dot at the upper right, before the word « ce », and a thin stroke runs from near B to the top vertex E of the second triangle; no stroke joins the dot to E, so there is no third closed triangle. Both strokes and the dot are now drawn (the thin one in pencil). Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: icosaèdre en perspective, sommets marqués $u, u', v, v', a, b$, faces hachurées.
drawings.notes: Icosahedron seen with a vertex in front: the hexagon of vertices (top T, upper right R, lower right V, bottom M = u', lower left, upper left) round the front vertices u, a, b; every edge is drawn between the same ten computed vertices. Heavy where he inked them: upper left - u, upper left - a, a - b. Edges drawn: T - upper left, T - R, u - upper left, u - R, u - b, a - b, a - upper left, a - u', b - u', b - V, R - V, upper left - lower left, lower left - u', u' - V; below, the faint lower half towards a bottom vertex: an arc from the lower left, a line from V, and a short stroke down from u' (and a short stroke down from T at the top). Hatched (as regular hatching, his is loose): the six faces round the hexagon (T-upper left-u, upper left-u-a, upper left-a-lower left, lower left-a-u', u'-b-V, b-V-R, u-R-b, T-u-R) and, faintly, the lower region; the two central faces u-a-b and a-b-u' are left blank, as on the page. A long faint curve over the top, from the left to beyond R, is drawn as a pencil curve (the old redraw closed it into an ellipse, which is not on the page). Labels as on the page: u, a, b, u', v (lower right), v' (lower left), v' (upper right, a reading); the label at the upper left (like "u?") is not readable and is left out; the faint letter under the bottom vertex, like "u", is drawn as a reading. Still differs: hatching is schematic; the two unreadable or faint labels. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the upper right label reads v' and the faint letter under the bottom vertex reads u; a faint u' also stands above the top vertex, just above the crop, and is now drawn, so that the labels down the axis read u', u, (a, b), u', u. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: plusieurs croquis de tétraèdres et d'octaèdres, en partie hachurés, sommets marqués $a, b, c, c', u$ ; un carré à diagonales ; le nombre 100 en marge.
drawings.kind: page of sketches of tetrahedra and octahedra
drawings.notes: Whole lower half of the page, ten small sketches redrawn each at its place (every edge between the same computed vertices): a square with both diagonals at the upper left (three corners as full dots, the lower right as an open dot, the diagonals stopping short of the corners, a second stroke under the bottom side); a tetrahedron with a heavy edge extended to a further vertex at the top (centre left); a square pyramid with one heavy edge and both base diagonals, with a stroke going off to the upper left (left); a tetrahedron with vertices a (top) and b (left), one edge heavy (centre left); a hatched sketch at the bottom left; a long bipyramid with a, b at its equator (bottom centre); the heavy sketch with c', a, b, c, u (centre right), two faces hatched; a hatched kite (below it); an open triangle and a small bipyramid (right). "100" in the margin. Hatching drawn as regular hatching. Left out: all the text of the page, the letter lists at the right (ac, bc, ab, c'a, c'b'...), a tiny letter in the lower tip of the long bipyramid, faint pencil strokes round the heavy sketch, and the struck horizontal stroke under it. Still differs: the small sketches are approximate at the scale of the page; the hidden edge of the centre-left tetrahedron and the inner diagonals of the left pyramid are readings. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the centre-left tetrahedron has its inner strokes (from the top vertex to an inner point and from there to the lower left corner) and the base of the left pyramid has its two crossing diagonals, all in ink on the page; they stay drawn. Not checked by a reader.
